Subsequent field investigation of the biogas conveyance system revealed that further sulfur removal did in fact occur in the biogas line that ran between the digesters and the waste gas flares.  The field investigation revealed that an inadvertently closed valve in the gas line had caused significant condensation to form in the pipe; Figure SI-3 replicates pictures taken during the field investigation, showing that sulfur deposits (seen as white in the photos) were found covering the bottom half and up to approximately the level of the “water line” of condensation as far away as 200 ft from the digester. This further substantiates the importance of gas phase RT for sulfur removal, as the volume of the gas line added to the total biogas “headspace” detention time resulting in the removal of sulfurous compounds from the biogas.
